text:
anya: Heads-up — conversion bug when bringing up hf://acme/spm-chat-1 -> redwood BPE. Special tokens end up shifted by +3 after merge rewrite, so chat templates insert wrong BOS/EOS and generation starts with garbage token IDs. Repro below.

devon: ugh. is this the sentencepiece->bpe script we added last month? any logs?

anya: yes, using tools/convert_spm_to_bpe.py from the onboarding repo. Repro steps:
```
# checkout model
git clone https://huggingface.co/acme/spm-chat-1
python tools/convert_spm_to_bpe.py --input spm-chat-1 --out redwood-tokenizer
# quick sanity check
head -n3 spm-chat-1/vocab.txt
head -n3 redwood-tokenizer/vocab.json
```
Observed: vocab.txt shows reserved tokens in front (
<pad> 0
<bos> 1
<eos> 2
), but resulting vocab.json has those tokens at 3,4,5 and indices 0..2 are opaque empty pieces created by SentencePiece when normalization split an empty joiner. Logs:
```
Conversion: detected nfkc normalizer -> applying.
Detected empty_piece entries: 3
Applied merge rewrite: offset +3 to all original token ids
```

kai: hmm this sounds like the classic empty-piece sentinel problem. SentencePiece can emit an empty-piece token which we then drop but forget to rebase indices. Did you run the merge-sort step that the script has?

anya: yes ran merge-sort. The issue reproduces only when the model uses non-canonical normalization form (NFKC vs NFC) and has suffixpiece entries that collapse to empty. The converter drops the empty pieces but applies a global offset to merge table without updating special token remap in config.json.

sophia: can you paste the small snippet showing the index discrepancy?

anya: sure:
```
# original spm vocab excerpt (index,value)
0 <pad>
1 <bos>
2 <eos>
3 ▁the
4 ▁and
# converted bpe vocab excerpt
0 ":empty_piece_0:"
1 ":empty_piece_1:"
2 ":empty_piece_2:"
3 <pad>
4 <bos>
5 <eos>
```

devon: yikes. That would break our chat templates because they expect <bos> id==1. Quick fix: remap special token ids in the tokenizer config to actual ids after conversion. But we should also fix converter so it keeps reserved tokens at front.

kai: proposed patch: when you drop empty pieces, compute id_map = {old_id: new_id} and then rewrite special_token_map in config.json before writing out. Example python: 
```
# after conversion
id_map = compute_id_map(old_vocab, new_vocab)
for k,v in cfg['special_tokens'].items():
    cfg['special_tokens'][k] = id_map.get(v, v)
write_config(cfg)
```

anya: I already hacked a local workaround that writes a remap table into tokenizer_config.json and adjusted chat template loader to prefer names over ids. It unblocks bring-up, but leaving this in place feels fragile.

model-converter-bot: Created issue #432 in redwood-inference/onboarding: "spm->bpe converter drops empty pieces and shifts special token ids" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/432).

devon: can you attach a minimal failing test? would like to add to CI. Also check quantization impact — I saw small tokenization differences blow up some evals earlier.

anya: attaching a tiny repro in the PR. Also ran int8 quant tests; perplexity on our eval set increases ~2.3% when using converted tokenizer without remap. With remap it's back to baseline.

kai: ok plan: 1) add unit test and failing case 2) implement id_map rewrite for special tokens 3) update converter to preserve reserved prefix when possible 4) add logging and a post-conversion validation step that ensures special token ids match expected names 5) add CI check that running convert -> encode(bos) -> decode produces original template prefix.

anya: +1 to all. I'll open the follow-up PR for the converter and link the test.

sophia: thanks — once merged we can re-run the quantization sweep and the eval harness. If regressions persist, we can also try keeping a small prefix-cache mapping during quant.

devon: perfect. :thumbsup:
